For the New Patriotic Party (NPP), as it prepares for the 2028 election, the case for Dr. Matthew Opoku Prempeh, popularly known as NAPO, deserves unequivocal support. results.title: La community heads to court over La Pleasure Beach demolition
results.content: The La community is preparing to challenge the demolition of structures at La Pleasure Beach in court, as its lawyer disputes the ownership of the land and warns against transferring it to an investor before the matter is resolved. Lawyer for La Pleasure Beach management and the affected business owners, Nsiah Akuetteh, says legal proceedings have begun to challenge the demolition, which took place on Friday, October 2. Mr Akuetteh has described the exercise as trespass, arguing that the land does not belong to those who carried out the demolition. He says the legal team will resist any attempt to hand the disputed property to an investor for development while questions over ownership remain unresolved. The demolition affected more than 85 businesses and over 4,000 people, leaving operators facing financial losses and uncertainty over their livelihoods.

results.title: The stadium is full, the nation is waiting
results.content: A single aerial photograph of the Accra Sports Stadium on the night of 17 October 2026 tells a story that no policy document has managed to tell as clearly: Ghana does not lack people who are willing to gather, to give, to wait, and to believe. What it lacks are institutions that young people trust enough to gather for. This article reads the ShattaFest crowd through the lenses of crowd psychology, the sociology of religion and development economics, names where the State and the Church have fallen short, and proposes a practical agenda for redirecting this extraordinary energy toward national development.
